headline: PM Tarique Rahman discusses expanding economic ties with Croatian PM
summary: The two leaders met on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly in New York to strengthen bilateral relations and trade.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenković held a bilateral meeting on Wednesday, September 23, in New York.
The meeting took place on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA)
The leaders discussed ways to strengthen the friendly bilateral relations between Bangladesh and Croatia, with a focus on expanding trade and investment.
They emphasized the need for mutual cooperation in key areas such as economic cooperation, skilled manpower, education, and technology.
Both prime ministers also discussed increasing coordination on international issues of common interest and enhancing cooperation within multilateral forums, including the United Nations.
caption:
Bangladesh and Croatia are looking to boost trade and investment. PM Tarique Rahman and Croatian PM Andrej Plenković met in New York to map out a new economic partnership.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenković held a bilateral meeting on Wednesday, September 23, in New York.

The meeting took place on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA)

The leaders discussed ways to strengthen the friendly bilateral relations between Bangladesh and Croatia, with a focus on expanding trade and investment.

They emphasized the need for mutual cooperation in key areas such as economic cooperation, skilled manpower, education, and technology.

Both prime ministers also discussed increasing coordination on international issues of common interest and enhancing cooperation within multilateral forums, including the United Nations.

Source: Jamuna TV, Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo

headline: PM Tarique Rahman unveils five-point plan to end Rohingya displacement at UN
summary: The Prime Minister called for concerted international action to ensure the safe, voluntary, and dignified return of refugees to Myanmar.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman presented a five-point plan at a high-level UN committee meeting co-hosted by Bangladesh and Gambia to address the Rohingya crisis.
He emphasized that Bangladesh has fulfilled its humanitarian duty and urged the international community to show the same resolve in creating conditions for the refugees' return to Myanmar.
The plan calls for a clear and credible roadmap for sustainable repatriation, demanding that violence against Rohingya and other civilians in Myanmar must cease immediately.
Tarique Rahman urged the international community to ensure predictable humanitarian assistance for both the refugees and the local host communities in Bangladesh.

The proposal highlights the need for justice and accountability, supporting the roles of the International Court of Justice and the International Criminal Court in holding those responsible for grave crimes accountable.
The Prime Minister also called for strengthened regional and international cooperation to combat cross-border crimes, including human trafficking, drug-based economies, and digital fraud.
He concluded by stating that the world must move from empathy to action, transitioning from managing displacement to bringing a permanent end to the crisis.
caption:
Bangladesh has carried its responsibility with humanity. Now the international community must carry its responsibility with conviction.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman presented a five-point plan at a high-level UN committee meeting co-hosted by Bangladesh and Gambia to address the Rohingya crisis.

He emphasized that Bangladesh has fulfilled its humanitarian duty and urged the international community to show the same resolve in creating conditions for the refugees' return to Myanmar.

The plan calls for a clear and credible roadmap for sustainable repatriation, demanding that violence against Rohingya and other civilians in Myanmar must cease immediately.

Tarique Rahman urged the international community to ensure predictable humanitarian assistance for both the refugees and the local host communities in Bangladesh.

The proposal highlights the need for justice and accountability, supporting the roles of the International Court of Justice and the International Criminal Court in holding those responsible for grave crimes accountable.

The Prime Minister also called for strengthened regional and international cooperation to combat cross-border crimes, including human trafficking, drug-based economies, and digital fraud.

He concluded by stating that the world must move from empathy to action, transitioning from managing displacement to bringing a permanent end to the crisis.
